s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive neurological disorder with gait disturbance, cognitive decline, and nonmotor symptoms
salient_findings: Progressive gait disturbance with imbalance and falls
Recent memory impairment and psychotic episodes
Rigid-akinetic syndrome with reduced speech output and emotional lability
key_facts: 78-year-old woman with no significant medical history
4-year history of progressive gait disturbance
Initial presentation with head tremor
Development of recent memory impairment and psychotic episodes 1 year after onset
Worsening walking disability requiring support for ambulation
Eventual wheelchair dependency
Nonmotor symptoms include reduced speech output, impaired comprehension, and emotional lability
Diffuse, generalized hyperintensity of supratentorial white matter on T2/FLAIR MRI sequences
Mildly elevated cerebrospinal fluid protein concentration
Normal cell count and glucose level in cerebrospinal fluid

shortlist.label: Progressive Supranuclear Palsy
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive gait disturbance, imbalance, and falls, with subsequent cognitive decline and nonmotor symptoms

shortlist.label: Corticobasal Degeneration
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive gait disturbance, rigidity, and cognitive decline, with asymmetric motor symptoms

shortlist.label: Multiple System Atrophy
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive gait disturbance, autonomic dysfunction, and cognitive decline, with parkinsonian features

shortlist.label: Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Rapidly progressive cognitive decline, with myoclonus, and diffuse white matter changes on MRI

shortlist.label: Frontotemporal Dementia
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive cognitive decline, with prominent nonmotor symptoms, and frontal lobe involvement

raw.rationale: The patient's progressive gait disturbance, initial head tremor, and subsequent development of recent memory impairment and psychotic episodes, along with the worsening walking disability and nonmotor symptoms, are consistent with Progressive Supranuclear Palsy. The diffuse, generalized hyperintensity of the supratentorial white matter on T2/FLAIR MRI sequences also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Corticobasal Degeneration
rejected.why: Lack of reported alien limb syndrome or significant asymmetric motor symptoms

rejected.label: Multiple System Atrophy
rejected.why: No mention of autonomic dysfunction or significant cerebellar ataxia

rejected.label: Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease
rejected.why: Negative tests for JC virus in the CSF and lack of rapid progression to death, which is typical for CJD

rejected.label: Frontotemporal Dementia
rejected.why: While the patient has memory impairment and psychotic episodes, the primary and progressive gait disturbance and other motor symptoms are more suggestive of Progressive Supranuclear Palsy
